newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Rates, profit slowdown to dampen US stocks.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Rates, profit slowdown to dampen US stocks.

text.p: A rise in interest rates and the possibility of firms failing to match earnings forecasts are expected to dampen U.S. stocks between now and the end of 1998, a Reuters poll showed on Wednesday.

Ten analysts who gave predictions for the Dow Jones Industrials put the index at around 7,100 by the end of this year, while the average prediction from nine analysts for the Nasdaq index averaged around 1,300.
On March 12, the last day of the survey, the Dow closed at 7,039.37 and the Nasdaq at 1,304.13.

Although the predictions are cautious, they are less bearish than in a survey three months ago, when the average outlook for the end of 1997 was for a six percent fall in both the Dow and Nasdaq indices.
Both indices have hit all-time closing highs since the last poll in December. The Dow reached 7,085 on March 11 and the Nasdaq hit 1,388.06 on January 22.
Analysts forecast cautious progress in the Dow for 1998, up to around 7,500 by the end of the year. The Nasdaq was seen barely changed at 1,340.
PETER CARDILLO, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH AT WESTFALIA INVESTMENTS:
"We will see an interest rate hike by the end of the year. Some companies will not live up to earnings expectations, and that is probably the main concern of the market.

"If we get a pre-emptive strike of 25 to 50 basis points from the Fed, and inflation does not accelerate to the point where more hikes are needed, it will be positive in the long term because you are taking action to curtail inflation."

"I think the Dow will hit 7200 by the year's end. Now, we are not that far away, but before then I think we will get a five to eight percent correction brought on by the fact that the market has been going up in a very narrow advance."
HARRY LAUBSCHER, MARKET ANALYST, TUCKER ANTHONY:
"The broader market is not looking good. A correction will hit the market fairly hard. Interest rates are going up, probably to 7.5 percent, and the market won't take that well."
GRAHAM TANAKA, PRESIDENT, TANAKA CAPITAL MANAGEMENT:
"The biggest reason we see for the increase is the huge continued inflows of savings that baby boomers are ploughing into the stock market."
ALFRED GOLDMAN, TECHNICAL ANALYST, A.G. EDWARDS, ST. LOUIS.
"Such projections ... are etched in sand, not in granite."

"If the Fed goes on a series of tightenings, give me a call back and I will adjust downward these projections. If the Fed does a symbolic 25-basis-point tightening, which I think is the worst case we've got in front of us, then it would only affect the market for a few hours."
